metadata.title: GLUE: A Multi-Task Benchmark and Analysis Platform for Natural Language Understanding

problem.statement: Most NLU models above the word level are designed for a specific task and struggle with out-of-domain data.
limitations_of_prior_work: Most NLU models above the word level are designed for a specific task.
Most NLU models struggle with out-of-domain data.

method.name: General Language Understanding Evaluation (GLUE)
method.key_idea: GLUE is a benchmark of nine diverse NLU tasks, an auxiliary dataset for probing models for understanding of specific linguistic phenomena, and an online platform for evaluating and comparing models.

components.name: Nine diverse NLU tasks
components.function: A suite of nine NLU tasks covering a broad range of domains, data quantities, and difficulties to spur development of generalizable NLU systems.

components.name: Diagnostic Dataset
components.function: A dataset of 550 hand-crafted NLI examples tagged with linguistic phenomena, designed to probe trained models for specific types of knowledge.

components.name: Online evaluation platform and leaderboard
components.function: A platform for evaluating and comparing models, primarily based on private test data to ensure fair usage.

key_findings: The best models still achieve fairly low absolute scores.
Analysis with our diagnostic dataset yields similarly weak performance over all phenomena tested, with some exceptions.
Experiments indicate that solving GLUE is beyond the capability of current transfer learning methods.

main_findings.claim: The Multi-task model achieved the highest average performance on the GLUE benchmark.
The Single-task model achieved an average score on the GLUE benchmark.
The CBoW model achieved an average score on the GLUE benchmark.
The Skip-Thought model achieved an average score on the GLUE benchmark.
The InferSent model achieved an average score on the GLUE benchmark.
The DisSent model achieved an average score on the GLUE benchmark.
The GenSen model achieved an average score on the GLUE benchmark.
The Multi-task model achieved the highest accuracy on SST-2.
The Multi-task model achieved the highest accuracy on QQP.
The Multi-task model achieved the highest Pearson correlation on STS-B.
The Multi-task model achieved the highest accuracy on QNLI.

contributions.description: A suite of nine NLU tasks, built on established annotated datasets and covering a diverse range of text genres, dataset sizes, and difficulties.
An online evaluation platform and leaderboard, based primarily on private test data.
An expert-constructed analysis dataset for probing models for understanding of specific linguistic phenomena.
Experiments indicate that solving GLUE is beyond the capability of current transfer learning methods.

comparisons.difference: Models trained with multi-task learning generally outperform models trained on a single benchmark task.
comparisons.evidence: Multi-task model achieved 69.0 Avg score vs. Single-task model's 64.8 Avg score.

comparisons.other_method: Pretrained models (CBoW, Skip-Thought, InferSent, DisSent, GenSen)
comparisons.difference: Models trained directly on the GLUE tasks generally outperform pretrained models.
comparisons.evidence: Multi-task model achieved 69.0 Avg score, higher than any pretrained model (e.g., GenSen 66.6 Avg).

limitations: Current transfer learning methods achieve fairly low absolute scores on the GLUE benchmark.
Current models show weak performance over all phenomena tested by the diagnostic dataset, with some exceptions.

key_terms.definition: A benchmark consisting of nine diverse NLU tasks, an auxiliary dataset for probing models for understanding of specific linguistic phenomena, and an online platform for evaluating and comparing models.
A dataset of hand-crafted NLI examples designed to highlight common linguistic phenomena (e.g., world knowledge, logical operators, lexical entailments) that models must grasp.
